title: Honey Balsamic Chicken Tenders
conventions: buy strings are cook measures (what goes in the pot). Grams are TARGET-scale: the mapper states them where its printed measure quantizes away from the exact scale, and otherwise they are parse-compute's source-basis weight for that line multiplied by scale_factor exactly once.

ingredients.buy: 5 1/4 lb, sliced on a diagonal into strips
ingredients.notes: Pre-resolve weighed this at 400 g on a 2-x-medium-breast each-weight, but the line states its own weight: 1.5 lb = 680 g. Source cost $2.99 for the line is $1.99/lb, which is a 1.5 lb buy, and 680 g over 4 servings is 170 g per serving, matching the catalog's 167 g chicken-breast average.

ingredients.buy: 3/4 cup plus 2 Tbsp, for the marinade
ingredients.notes: 14 Tbsp = 224 g at 3.5x; marinade portion, kept separate from the pan-sauce balsamic.
1 clove x 3.5 = 3.5 cloves; rounded up to 4 whole cloves so the printed countable and the grams agree (12 g at batch scale).
Half goes in the marinade, half in the skillet, per the method.

Table carried 20 g at source basis, which is 70 g at batch scale - about 3 1/2 Tbsp of salt for 14 servings. Reset to the live-catalog precedent of ~15 g per finished 14-serving batch (4.3 g source basis). Salt line only.
Table's 4 g is the FINISHED-batch precedent figure, not source basis; at source basis it would print 14 g of pepper. Reset to 1.2 g source = ~4 g per 14-serving batch. Pepper line only.
Second balsamic line; deglazes the skillet after the chicken comes out.
10 1/2 Tbsp = 220 g at 3.5x; 2/3 cup is the closest measure a cook holds (224 g).

macro_cross_check.verdict: pre-computed figures do NOT stand - the main protein line was under-weighed by 280 g
